impl:BE-08.summary:
Blocked before any change: "GET /accounts/{id}/export includes the rows" needs a new field on AccountExportOut, which lives in the account LIBRARY (/home/user/account/src/main/java/ai/carmonai/account/AccountExportOut.java), outside my HOLD (only /home/user/account-service). account-service's AccountResource implements the library's AccountController, which returns ResponseEntity<AccountExportOut> (a final record with only account, organizations, exportedAt). The service therefore cannot add the acceptance rows to the export response, and the IT (which reads the export through the library's Feign client) could not assert them. I changed nothing and made no commit; account-service's working tree is clean on claude/peaceful-turing-14vw06.

The rest of BE-08 fits inside account-service and I have mapped it: migration V2026.10.13.001__terms_acceptance.sql, creating accounts.terms_acceptance(account_id, document CHECK in ('terms','privacy'), version, accepted_at, channel). It would be append-only through refuse_change() with BEFORE UPDATE OR DELETE and BEFORE TRUNCATE triggers, like billing's V2026.10.03.001. Because that function name is per-schema, the migration must create it in schema accounts. The table gets no foreign key to account, so erasure does not cascade. COMMENT ON TABLE would state evidence of acceptance, retention, and that erasure leaves the rows because they hold only the account id, flagged as an assumption for the lawyer (BUS-10). The Java side would be a TermsAcceptanceModel, a repository, AccountService.recordTermsAcceptance(...) (blank or missing versions throw IllegalArgumentException, which the existing handler maps to 400) and an export() extension. The ITs would cover the 400, the row and the export, UPDATE/DELETE/TRUNCATE refusal, and rows surviving DELETE /accounts/{id}.

Smallest unblock: re-dispatch with /home/user/account added to HOLD, to add `List<TermsAcceptance> termsAcceptances` (record: document, version, acceptedAt, channel) to AccountExportOut and then `install` it. Alternatively, accept an export-less BE-08 and move the export part elsewhere.

On your question "why is docker not available?": it is available here. The daemon is running (server 29.8.2, /var/run/docker.sock present, `docker ps` works). The postgres, valkey and mailpit images show as `<none>` tag in `docker images` because they were loaded by digest only. The postgres digest 639ab7ce... matches the one hard-coded in AccountServiceIT. Docker is not what blocked this task.

tests.result: Not run: no code changed because the task is blocked on the library export DTO.
tests.notRun: New acceptance tests were not written. The mvn -B -pl api/account-service verify run was not performed. Docker itself is not the obstacle.

deviations: No work done: the export requirement cannot be met inside the allowed HOLD (account-service only).
followUps: Add termsAcceptances to AccountExportOut in the account library (needs a HOLD on /home/user/account), then re-run BE-08 with both repos.

The pre-pulled images carry no tags, only digests; if any tool resolves them by tag (e.g. `docker run postgres:17.11-bookworm`), it will not find them locally. The ITs use the image@digest form, so they work.
The guide cites AccountService.java:141-166 for the export. In this code the export method is at about lines 130-147, so the pass-2 line numbers are off.

impl:BE-06.summary:
BE-06 is implemented and committed in both repos, and both modules verify green. On your question: Docker was available throughout this run, so I found nothing to fix. `docker version` answered for client and server (29.8.2), dockerd was running, and the Testcontainers ITs started Postgres and Valkey and passed. The postgres, valkey and mailpit images show as `<none>` in `docker images`, but they are present under the exact digests `BillingServiceIT` pins. If you saw "docker not available" somewhere else, it was not in this sandbox. Send me that output if you want it chased.

What changed:
- **Library:** `GrantIn` gains `type` and `reference`. Old JSON with neither field still works, and so does JSON with explicit nulls.
- **Service:** `type` defaults to `grant`; `grant` and `top_up` are the only other accepted value, and anything else (including empty or `TOP_UP`) is a 400 through the existing `IllegalArgumentException` to `ProblemDetail` handler. `reference` falls back to `reason` when null; a blank or over-256 value is a 400.
- **Fixed error text:** the error messages are fixed text and never echo the rejected value.
- **Ledger row:** it now stores the requested type and reference.
- **Idempotency:** the key is still `grant:{org}:{idempotencyKey}`, so a replay leaves one row and one balance increase.
- **Comments:** `GrantIn` and `BillingService.grant` now say the key is the Pix end-to-end id and the reference is the id plus an operator tag, never a payer name. Nothing logs the reference.
- **Credit flag:** the existing `flags.sync` already clears `no_credit` synchronously after the commit, so no fix was needed. The new IT proves it clears within 1 s of the top-up answer.
- **Migration:** none; the ledger CHECK already allows `top_up` and the table already has `reference`.

The 5 new ITs plus one typed-client test are in `BillingServiceIT`. The 5 raw-JSON ones all failed on unchanged code. The typed-client test (`theClientLibraryCarriesTypeAndReference`) could not compile before the change, so it was added afterwards.

tests.command: cd /home/user/ws && mvn -B -pl api/billing verify; mvn -B -q -pl api/billing -DskipTests install; mvn -B -pl api/billing-service verify
tests.result: mvn -B -pl api/billing verify: BUILD SUCCESS (the library has no tests, so no Tests run line). mvn -B -pl api/billing-service verify: PriceTest 'Tests run: 3, Failures: 0, Errors: 0, Skipped: 0'; BillingServiceIT 'Tests run: 14, Failures: 0, Errors: 0, Skipped: 0'; BUILD SUCCESS.

Five new cases failed, for example aTopUpIsOneTypedAndReferencedLedgerRowAndItsReplayChangesNothing: ['type'='grant' (expected: 'top_up')], refusesAnyOtherType... [type 'refund'] expected: 400 but was: 200, and aReferenceOfExactlyTheLimitIsKept: expected the 256-character reference but was: 'test'.
tests.notRun: bash docker/revenue-check.sh and the full compose stack (not available in this code line and excluded by the task). The independent money review (PRV-10) is not done.

deviations: `reason` stays required (1 to 200 characters) even when `reference` is sent, because the task did not say to relax it and the existing validation and 400 message are unchanged. A top-up caller must still send a reason.
A blank or empty `reference` is a 400. Only null or absent falls back to `reason`, so a missing Pix id cannot be silently replaced.
A replayed idempotency key with a different type or reference is not an error: the first write wins and the replay returns the balance. This follows from ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING and is not tested.

The guide's reconcile `balanced:true` and `docker/revenue-check.sh` do not exist in this code line. Reconcile only logs. The ITs assert `repository.mismatches()` does not contain the organization, which is the same check.
Validation was not extracted, so there is no separate GrantIn unit test. It lives in `BillingService.grant` and is covered by the ITs.
Every request ID reference in the guide (BE-24 shared secret, HOST-06) is not implemented here; the endpoint's protection was not touched.
I ran `mvn install` for `api/billing`, as the task instructs. That puts the new, backwards-compatible `GrantIn` into the shared ~/.m2 for other workers.
followUps: Consider making `reason` optional when `reference` is present, since the ledger only stores the reference.
BillingResource's ProblemDetail handler returns `e.getMessage()`. It is safe today because all messages are fixed text, but a fixed-text mapping would match the project rule more strictly.

The existing IT `billsEachSealedWindowOnceAndFlagsOrganizationsOutOfCredit` asserts a global `mismatches()` is empty, which depends on test order because another test leaves drift on purpose. Scope it to its organizations.

blockers.issue: The closure can be bypassed, so SEC-01 is not met: the filter compares the raw string `exchange.getRequest().getPath().value()` to `/auth/register` with equals(), but the route predicate and the security matcher match decoded path segments. I ran the real gateway (real filter chain, security, routing, with a stub auth) in a scratch copy and sent raw requests. `POST /auth/%72egister` returned 202 and reached the stub as `POST /auth/%72egister`. `POST /auth/register` returned 403 and the stub got 0 calls. A real Tomcat/Spring MVC app also maps `/auth/%72egister` to the `/auth/register` handler (checked with a scratch app on the same Boot 4.1.0), and auth-service has no servlet Spring Security firewall. So anyone who can reach the published port 8080 can still create accounts and trigger the verification mail: the gateway fails open on an encoded path. `;` matrix parameters (`/auth/register;a=b`) are not stopped by this filter either; the gateway happened to answer 400 for them in my run, but the equals() check does not stop them. OriginFilter has the same equals() pattern for its paths (pre-existing, not in this diff).
blockers.fix: Match with the same PathPattern semantics the router and security use, not string equality. In RegistrationFilter: `static final PathPattern PATH = new PathPatternParser().parse("/auth/register");` and test `PATH.matches(exchange.getRequest().getPath().pathWithinApplication())`. Optionally call `setMatchOptionalTrailingSeparator(true)` on the parser. I applied exactly this in the scratch copy and re-ran the raw-socket probe: `/auth/register`, `/auth/%72egister`, `/auth/register;a=b`, `/auth/register;` and `/auth/register?x=1` all return 403 registration_closed with 0 stub calls, `/auth/login` still passes, and RegistrationFilterTest still compiles and passes. Add unit cases for the encoded and `;` forms.

blockers.issue: The spec's test (BE-03 step 1 and Done-when: new GatewayIT cases) is missing. GatewayIT does not exist in gateway-service or in back, now or in history, and the diff adds none. Only a unit test of `new RegistrationFilter(false)` against a MockServerWebExchange was added. No test starts a Spring context, so the following are never tested: the application.yaml default (`registration-open` = false: changing it to `true` fails no test), the @Component registration and ordering ahead of security and routing, the claim that the auth/account stub gets 0 calls, and that `registration-open=true` returns 202. This is why the bypass above went unnoticed: an HTTP-level test would have failed on `/auth/%72egister`. The spec requires 403 with defaults, 0 backend calls (mail is sent only by the backend, so 0 calls proves no mail), and 202 when open.
blockers.fix: Add a `@SpringBootTest(webEnvironment = RANDOM_PORT)` test (GatewayIT, or a similarly named class if the repo's failsafe pattern needs it). Use a JDK HttpServer or WireMock stub as the auth route target via DynamicPropertySource: `spring.cloud.gateway.server.webflux.routes[0].uri` plus the matching predicate, and VALKEY_* dummies. Case 1: default properties; `POST /auth/register`, `POST /auth/%72egister` and `POST /auth/register;x=1` all return 403 with a body containing `registration_closed`, and the stub counter stays 0. Also assert `POST /auth/login` still reaches the stub. Case 2: `carmonai.gateway.registration-open=true`; `POST /auth/register` returns 202 and the stub counter is 1. Send raw sockets or a WebTestClient with an encoded URI so the path is not normalized by the client. My scratch BypassProbeTest in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-back/25b509fc-e88c-57fe-9898-f37ad4528f80/scratchpad/gw is a working skeleton for this.

nits: Docker was not available here, so smoke.sh with the property on (spec Done-when, PRV-05) and the production-compose curl returning 403 were not run. Only compose.yaml (the harness) exists in back, so HOST-06's production compose is not checked. The compose change itself is correct: it sets the variable on the gateway service in the harness compose only, and the name matches the yaml placeholder CARMONAI_GATEWAY_REGISTRATIONOPEN.

The back commit changes only docker/compose.yaml; the api/gateway-service gitlink in back still points at cb417d2, not 44e6a9d. Until the parent pointer is bumped (pass-2 step 5), the parent's CI and compose build a gateway without the filter.

Failure modes checked and fine: the key is absent only if removed from the yaml, which makes startup fail (fail closed); a malformed or empty env value also fails startup rather than opening registration. The 403 body is a fixed string. AccessLogFilter logs only method, path, status and ids, no body or email. There is no race or idempotency surface: it is static config with no state.
Optional hardening: when closed, deny every method on the path, not only POST. Today other methods are 401 unauthenticated, or 404/405 from auth when authenticated, so this is not exploitable.

OriginFilter has the same raw-equality weakness on /auth/login, /auth/register, /auth/refresh and /auth/logout: an encoded path skips the Origin (CSRF) check. Pre-existing and out of this task's scope, but the PathPattern fix could be shared in one helper.

Documentation: docs/services/gateway.md and docs/internals/fact-sheet.md list the gateway filters and do not mention RegistrationFilter or the new property. docs/reference/gaps.md still says registration works.
review:BE-03.testsProveClaim: No. RegistrationFilterTest proves only that `new RegistrationFilter(false)` refuses the exact string /auth/register and passes other literal paths. It would fail if the filter logic were removed or inverted. It does not prove the claim that nobody can create accounts through the gateway: it never runs the real HTTP stack and it does not test the yaml default of false or the wiring and order. The real gateway still lets `POST /auth/%72egister` through to the auth backend, and the unit tests stay green. The spec's GatewayIT cases (403, 0 backend calls, 202 when open) are absent."

nits: Every spec acceptance point in the diff is met. GrantIn has optional type and reference. type is grant (default) or top_up and anything else is a 400. reference is 1 to 256 characters. The key format grant:{org}:{key} is kept. The write is one transaction (insert plus balance), so a replay writes nothing. Error text is fixed and never echoes type or reference. The reference is never logged. There is no gateway route to /billing, and the billing container sits on the internal network with no published port. An absent or typo'd type falls to grant, which is the safe direction.

top_up without reference is accepted and stores the free-text reason as the reference (BillingService.grant). The spec goal says a top_up row carries the Pix id, and reason is free text that could hold a payer name in an append-only table. The Pix id still lands in idempotency_key, so traceability is not lost. Consider require(!"top_up".equals(type) || reference != null, ...) and, optionally, a charset or prefix check that the reference starts with the idempotencyKey.

A replay with a different amount, type or reference returns 200 and the old balance, silently dropping the new payload (documented in the code comment, untested). A 409 on a mismatched replay would stop an operator from believing a Pix was credited when it was not. The spec fixes the key format, so this is optional.

The key is scoped per organization (spec-mandated). The same Pix end-to-end id can therefore be credited to two organizations if an operator retries with a wrong org id, and the ledger cannot catch it. organizationId is only length-checked, so ids containing ':' could theoretically collide ('a:b'+'c' vs 'a'+'b:c'). Validate organizationId as a UUID. SELL-03 should guard the one-Pix-one-org rule.

Spec step 1 says 'reconcile returns balanced:true'. The tests call repository.mismatches() and assert the balance amount directly, which is equivalent in effect. billing.reconcile() is void and no reconcile endpoint exists in billing-service, although back/docs/services/billing.md describes GET /actuator/reconcile. mismatches() also uses a LEFT JOIN from balance, while the docs describe a FULL OUTER JOIN. That is a pre-existing gap, outside this diff.

The 'Done when' command bash docker/revenue-check.sh cannot run: /home/user/back/docker/revenue-check.sh does not exist at HEAD (f5a4bee) and was never in history. The 'review verdict recorded in PRV-10' step is still open.

Documentation: the Pix-id-as-idempotency-key rule is in the GrantIn and BillingService comments. The BillingController Feign javadoc, back/docs/services/billing.md (still lists the 4-field GrantIn and 'writes one grant entry'), and the back submodule pointers for billing and billing-service are not updated. Follow-up for the orchestrator.

Rollout order: an old billing-service replica ignores unknown JSON fields (Boot default), so a new caller sending type=top_up to an old replica would silently book a grant. Deploy billing-service before any caller that sends top_up (SELL-03).
POST /billing/grants has no application-layer auth until BE-24. top_up rows (cash received) are mintable by anything on the internal network. Land BE-24 before SELL-03 goes live.

Pre-existing, not introduced here: flags.sync(balance) runs after the commit on a snapshot. A concurrent debit can be overwritten by a stale grant snapshot until the 10-minute reconcile. There is also no concurrent same-key test (the unique index plus ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING handles it correctly).
review:BE-06.testsProveClaim:
Yes. I ran BillingServiceIT in a scratch copy of billing-service against the real Postgres and Valkey containers (digest-pinned images, JDK 25), and the repos were not modified. Baseline: 14 of 14 pass. Mutations of the service code:

- Ignoring type and reference (always grant, reference = reason) fails 5 new tests: aTopUpIsOneTypedAndReferenced..., aTopUpThatLiftsAnExhausted..., theClientLibraryCarriesTypeAndReference, anExplicitGrantTypeIsAccepted and aReferenceOfExactlyTheLimitIsKept.
- Removing the type check fails refusesAnyOtherType... (at 'refund') and theClientLibraryCarriesTypeAndReference.
- Removing the reference check fails refusesAnyOtherType... (at the 1-character blank reference).
- Raising the reference limit from 256 to 300 fails the same test at the 257-character case.

Together with the body-level assertions that nothing is written on a refusal (no ledger rows, no balance row), the tests would fail if the change were removed. They also fail on the original code, where the new GrantIn fields do not compile and the wire-level tests see type 'grant' with reference 'test'. Not covered: a concurrent same-key replay, a replay carrying a different payload, and a top_up with no reference.

On your question of why docker is not available: in this environment it is available now. `docker info` answers, and dockerd (pid 2606, overlay2) has been running since 13:58. /var/run/docker.sock is root:docker mode 660 and I run as root. fix:BE-03.summary: Fixed both blockers in gateway-service. (1) RegistrationFilter now matches with a PathPattern("/auth/register") against pathWithinApplication(), the same semantics as the router and security, so /auth/%72egister, /auth/r%65gister, /auth/register;a=b, /auth/register; and /auth/register?x=1 are all 403 registration_closed with 0 backend calls. (2) Added GatewayIT (@SpringBootTest RANDOM_PORT, real filter chain, security and routing, JDK HttpServer stub as the auth route, raw-socket requests so paths are not normalized): default properties give 403 on all the forms above with stub counter 0; /auth/login still reaches the stub; with registration-open=true POST /auth/register returns 202 and the stub gets 1 call. Mutation check: flipping the application.yaml default to true makes GatewayIT fail. Added unit cases for encoded and matrix forms in RegistrationFilterTest. The back repo needed no change (its earlier commit only sets the harness compose property) so there is no commit there. Docker was available and running throughout (docker ps works; Testcontainers images up), so the question "why is docker not available" does not apply to this environment.

added: GatewayIT (nested RegistrationClosedByDefault x3 cases, RegistrationOpen x1)

deviations: gateway-service/pom.xml: added maven-failsafe-plugin (version managed by the Boot parent, same declaration as account-service) so GatewayIT runs in verify; gateway had no failsafe before. No new dependency.

The reviewer's optional setMatchOptionalTrailingSeparator(true) does not exist in this Spring version (compile error), so it is not used. Trailing-slash forms (/auth/register/) are not matched by the router or security either: the gateway answers 401 itself and the stub gets 0 calls; GatewayIT asserts that (status in 401/403/404, 0 backend calls) instead of 403.

The guide's check that no mail reaches Mailpit is covered indirectly: the mail is sent only by the backend and the stub proves 0 backend calls; no Mailpit container is involved in this gateway-level IT.
The IT uses a JDK HttpServer stub rather than WireMock to avoid a new dependency; VALKEY_* are dummies since Lettuce connects lazily.
followUps: OriginFilter has the same string-equality path check (Set.contains on getPath().value()) for /auth/login, /auth/register, /auth/refresh, /auth/logout: an encoded path such as /auth/%6Cogin skips the Origin check. Pre-existing and out of scope here; fix with PathPattern matching and an IT.
